executive_summary.headline: Feeds are becoming something you talk to
executive_summary.body: Facebook now lets people type what they want into Your algorithm, and large language models re-rank Feed and Reels in real time. Instagram and Threads already had versions, so this is turning into a standard control.

executive_summary.headline: Platforms are paying small creators and sellers directly
executive_summary.body: LinkedIn added a pre-roll revenue share and paid Advice Sessions, TikTok Shop UK added photo carousels, LIVE deals and Subscribe & Save, and Buffer put $25,600 behind an API build contest.

executive_summary.headline: Cheap, open creative models land on gaming hardware
executive_summary.body: FLUX 3 Image Klein ships 5.6B open weights for 8 GB GPUs with free commercial use under $5M revenue, while Krea 3 and MVLAND Music Ads aim at fast edits and 30-second product ads.

top_picks.title: Facebook lets people steer Feed and Reels by typing what they want
top_picks.summary: Facebook introduced Your algorithm, a space in the three-dot menu where people add and manage topics for Feed and Reels in their own words. Follow-up questions after 'Interested' or 'Not interested' refine the ranking, and large language models let recommendations adapt in real time.
top_picks.author: Meta
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal the idea of letting the audience tell the system what they want in plain words. Try a one-question 'what do you want more of?' poll at the end of your next newsletter or internal demo and sort next month's topics by the answers.
top_picks.why_it_matters: The same natural-language steering has now appeared on Instagram and Threads, so it is becoming a default feed pattern.

top_picks.title: An AI creator calls Meta Muse's 'ideas' tab the best use-case generator she has tried
top_picks.summary: The post says Muse's 'ideas' tab reads your own context and pitches specific things to try, instead of the usual vacation, meal-plan and workout prompts. The author rates the ideas as roughly 20x better than other labs' suggestions, which is her opinion rather than a measured result.
top_picks.author: Allie K. Miller
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal the 'AI pitches you ideas from your own context' loop. Try it on your own week: paste your calendar and to-do list into any assistant and ask for five things you have not thought to automate.

top_picks.title: Edits adds tappable audio links, Kits for saved styles and a trending-topics view
top_picks.summary: Edits now lets Reels creators attach tappable links to songs and sounds, save visual style combinations as Kits and see trending topics (for accounts above 10,000 followers), plus more visual effects.
top_picks.author: Andrew Hutchinson
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal the 'save your look as a preset' habit. Try building your own Kit for a recurring video format, like a weekly update, so every episode starts from one tap.
top_picks.recurrence_note: Edits assistant was last week's pick; this week adds audio links, Kits and trending topics.

top_picks.title: LinkedIn starts paying creators with pre-roll ad revenue share and paid Advice Sessions
top_picks.summary: LinkedIn announced In-Stream Ads (invite-only US test, split undisclosed), Advice Sessions (paid 1:1 calls from a profile, no LinkedIn cut, US Business Premium) and a creator dashboard rolling out globally.
top_picks.author: Charu Mitra Dubey
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal the 'post here, get paid here' model: a profile that sells a 20-minute expert call. Try offering one bookable office-hours slot per week and see which topics get booked first.

top_picks.title: Buffer opens a build contest with a $25,600 prize pool for apps on its API
top_picks.summary: Buffer Commit awards 10% of August net profit ($25,600) to up to 16 apps built on the Buffer API. Registration opens Oct 15, the build window runs Oct 28 to Nov 13, and winners are announced Dec 7.
top_picks.author: Sabreen Haziq
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal the public build-contest format as a way to surface good ideas fast. Try a two-week internal 'build on our data' sprint with a small prize and a demo day.

top_picks.title: TikTok Shop UK turns photo carousels into shoppable posts and adds group deals in LIVE
top_picks.summary: UK sellers can publish shoppable carousels from two or more images (five to seven recommended), run Group Deal, Price Cut and Second Chance in LIVE, mix auction and fixed-price selling, and reserve stock for streams.
top_picks.author: Andrew Hutchinson
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal the 'no video needed' format: turn photos you already have into a swipeable post with a buy button. Try five to seven product photos in order, with the best-seller first.

top_picks.title: Google.org funds 17 AI-for-science teams with $36M, from fusion modeling to sodium-ion batteries
top_picks.summary: Recipients include teams training agents to read microscopy images for automated materials discovery, physics-informed models of fusion reactors, and AI forecasting of battery cathode wear. Each can join a six-month accelerator with engineering support and compute.
top_picks.author: Google.org
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal the 'agent reads the lab images so humans decide' pattern. Try pointing a vision model at a folder of your own inspection or product photos and ask it to sort them into three bins.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Science bonus +0.5 applied: materials-discovery and battery projects use agents on real experimental data.

sections.title: LinkedIn
sections.description: Creator money tools and practitioner posts from the week.

items.title: Sort agent work into three buckets to decide when it should interrupt you
items.summary: The post suggests asking how bad it is if the agent gets it wrong: easy to undo and unseen, let it act; easy to undo but sent in your name, draft and wait; hard to undo, bring it to you. Tasks move up a bucket as drafts keep coming back good.
items.author: Allie K. Miller
items.enterprise_translation: Steal the three-bucket sort for any assistant you run. Try labelling your next ten recurring tasks 1, 2 or 3 and let the agent loose on only the 1s this week.

items.title: A four-lens routine for forecasting AI: research, startups, public mood and policy
items.summary: The post lays out a forecasting habit built on arXiv for research, Y Combinator and Hacker News for startups, TikTok comments for public mood, and policy news for friction. It asks readers to pick one prediction and run all four lenses on it.
items.author: Allie K. Miller
items.enterprise_translation: Steal the four-lens checklist for any prediction. Try picking one question, like 'when will my favorite tool do X?', and write one line per lens on Friday.

items.title: Agents that ask for refunds and cancel subscriptions could remove 'forgot to cancel' revenue
items.summary: The post imagines millions of agents requesting refunds and contesting charges, and suggests subscription businesses assume 40% of paying inactive users disappear within two years. The figure is the author's estimate.
items.author: Allie K. Miller
items.enterprise_translation: Steal the 'design for the user who pays attention' mindset. Try rewriting one onboarding email so it earns the renewal with a result the customer can see.

items.title: LinkedIn tests a Network feed and adds pinned comments, digital business cards and expertise filters
items.summary: Alongside the money tools, LinkedIn is testing a Network feed (India included) and adding pinned comments, digital business cards, private profile notes and expertise filters in the Creator Marketplace.
items.author: Charu Mitra Dubey
items.enterprise_translation: Steal the pinned-comment move: put the link or next step in the first reply. Try pinning a one-line 'start here' comment under your best-performing post.

sections.title: TikTok
sections.description: Seller and creator commerce tools this week.

items.title: TikTok Shop UK LIVE gets Group Deal, Price Cut, Second Chance and Multi Selling Mode
items.summary: Group Deal and Price Cut unlock a lower price when a group sales target is met, Second Chance re-offers an auction item to the next-highest bidders, and sellers can mix auction and fixed-price items in one stream with reserved inventory.
items.author: Andrew Hutchinson
items.enterprise_translation: Steal the 'everyone wins when the room hits the goal' mechanic. Try a shared target in your next live session, where reaching 100 viewers unlocks a bonus demo.

items.title: TikTok Shop UK adds Subscribe & Save at 5 to 20% off and an automated ad program for unadvertised products
items.summary: Subscribe & Save lets buyers set recurring purchases at 5, 10, 15 or 20% off, which sellers can edit or pause. GMV Max Net Sales Boost creates and optimizes ads for eligible products not yet advertised, free for the first 30 days.
items.author: Dragomir Stojkov
items.enterprise_translation: Steal the repeat-order discount ladder. Try offering a 10% 'send me this every month' option on your top consumable and watch which tier people choose.

sections.title: Instagram
sections.description: Reels and Edits creation tools this week.

items.title: Instagram adds 'Use as reference' to overlay another Reel while you record
items.summary: For Reels under 90 seconds, the three-dot menu now offers 'Use as reference', which opens the Reel in a small movable window in the camera so creators can watch it as often as needed while recording a response.
items.author: Andrew Hutchinson
items.enterprise_translation: Steal the picture-in-picture response format. Try recording your next explainer while a reference clip plays in the corner so your pacing matches the original.

sections.title: Facebook and Meta
sections.description: Feed controls are in Top Picks; Meta's new model release is below.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder with Active Memory and Active Focus for personal and work agents
items.summary: Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full target agent tasks, memory and coding. Muse Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code; Full is for Muse Code subscribers, and Muse Wonder will later power experiences in the Muse app.
items.author: Meta AI Research
items.enterprise_translation: Steal the 'memory plus keep-going' pairing as a checklist for any assistant. Try giving your current tool a one-page 'what matters to me' note and a stretch goal, then compare the results to a cold start.

items.title: YouTube tests Ask YouTube inside the Shorts player
items.summary: A limited, English-only test lets viewers aged 18 and over ask questions about the Short they are watching, and new mobile feeds help viewers find similar creators.
items.author: Matt G. Southern
items.enterprise_translation: Steal the 'ask the video a question' interaction. Try adding a pinned FAQ comment to your next video that answers the three questions viewers ask most.

sections.title: Creator and Indie Tools
sections.description: Image and ad-creative tools that small teams and solo makers can use now.

items.title: FLUX 3 Image Klein: 5.6B open-weights image model that runs on 8 GB GPUs
items.summary: Black Forest Labs released a 5.6B-parameter model for text-to-image, editing with up to 10 reference images and bounding-box layout control. Commercial use is free under $5M annual revenue, and API pricing starts at $0.008 per image.
items.author: Black Forest Labs
items.enterprise_translation: Steal the 'reference images plus boxes' control for layout-true visuals. Try placing three product photos in a layout with boxes and generating a banner locally on a gaming laptop.

items.title: Krea 3 launches in beta with fast regional edits and multi-reference editing
items.summary: Krea 3 is an image generation and editing model; vendor materials describe 2K edits in under 8 seconds, bounding-box edits and up to 8 references.
items.author: Krea
items.enterprise_translation: Steal the 'edit one region, keep the rest' workflow. Try a sketch-to-render session where you box a single object and swap it five ways.

items.title: MVLAND Music Ads turns a product image and selling points into a 30-second music video ad
items.summary: The feature from MVLAND, a Meitu music video generator, takes product images and key selling points and produces a music-driven 30-second ad in three steps, aimed at independent sellers and small brands.
items.author: MVLAND
items.enterprise_translation: Steal the 'benefits as lyrics' idea. Try turning your product's three selling points into a four-line jingle and posting it as a 15-second clip.

sections.title: AI for Science
sections.description: Research that points to new materials, batteries and energy.

items.title: MIT model lets AI 'see' 3D crystal structures alongside text to rank battery and other materials
items.summary: A Nature Communications paper combines 3D atomic structures with natural-language descriptions from papers and computational databases. Asked for solid-state lithium-ion battery electrolytes, its top results included materials independently flagged as promising.
items.author: Zach Winn
items.enterprise_translation: Steal the 'pair the picture with the paragraph' trick. Try giving a model both a photo and your written notes for the same item and ask which one it trusts for each detail.
items.why_it_matters: Science bonus +0.5 applied: peer-reviewed materials-discovery method.

LinkedIn's In-Stream Ads and Advice Sessions (Oct 15) and Buffer Commit's $25,600 pool (Oct 15) both put revenue behind small makers.

emerging_signals.pattern: Open-weights creative models on consumer GPUs
emerging_signals.evidence: FLUX 3 Image Klein runs on 8 GB of video memory with API prices from $0.008 per image (Oct 15).

emerging_signals.pattern: Agent autonomy sorted by how reversible the work is
emerging_signals.evidence: A widely shared LinkedIn post (Oct 18) proposes three buckets from act-alone to ask-first, matching the Muse Wonder release's emphasis on agents that check in before important actions (Oct 12).

emerging_signals.pattern: Agents that read lab images and 3D structure speed materials discovery
emerging_signals.evidence: Google.org funded 17 AI-for-science teams (Oct 14) and an MIT multimodal crystal model was published in Nature Communications (Oct 18).

suggested_refinements.notes: Source gaps: LinkedIn post pages are blocked by robots.txt and show no reaction counts, so LinkedIn posts were read through a curated mirror (georges.blog) with the LinkedIn URL as a secondary link; no engagement numbers were captured. Direct TikTok and Instagram creator feeds, hashtag sweeps and view counts were not reachable without a browser session, so no current-week creator Reel or TikTok video was verified and the engagement field is omitted. Facebook groups were not accessible. The TikTok section has 2 items and the Instagram section has 1 beyond the Top Picks because only these were verifiable in the Oct 12-18 window; the Oct 5 TikTok Advertising Week items and Edits assistant are last week's. Mollick posts are X-based and belong to the X tab. Risk, safety and regulation stories (LinkedIn AI-slop reporting, TikTok AI-content controls, YouTube Music AI labels, Deezer AI filter, a political-ad study, Meta bot-access terms, a deleted-season story) were routed to the Research tab.
